chapter: Chicago and New York with Louis Armstrong, 1925-30
title: Don Redman arranging for Louis in Chicago
summary: Louis wanted Don Redman, then handling the Gold Coast Kette bands out of McKinney's Cotton Pickers, to write arrangements for the band; the tape ends.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well how did Don Redman come in on that?
Well Don Redman made some arrangements for us.
Yes, but I mean, did you all go to Detroit?
No he came from New York.
I know he came from Detroit, but I didn't know about Donald Redman. I listened to that band.
For Louis. Louis wanted Donald Redman to come and make some arrangements for us. band
Because what/was it Don Redman was in?
McKinney's Cotton Pickers and Louis likes that style.

Because like Don Redman was handling all the Gold Kette outfits at that time. See, and so when, when Don would come to Chicago to rehearse one of the Gold Kette bands that's when Louis got the idea to have Don Redman to come in and......
We've got to stop. Just rest. That was part of Chicago at that time.
